title.zh: 卷六十九 列傳第十九: 侯君集 張亮 薛萬徹
title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 19: Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche
title.raw: 卷六十九 列傳第十九: 侯君集 張亮 薛萬徹 Volume 69 Biographies 19: Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche

sentences.zh: 侯君集 張亮 薛萬徹 兄萬均 盛彥師 盧祖尚 劉世讓 劉蘭 李君羨等附

translations.literal: Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche, his elder brother Wan Jun, Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, Li Junxian, and others—appended.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Hou Junji, Zhang Liang, Xue Wanche, Xue Wanche's elder brother Wan Jun, Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, Li Junxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 侯君集，豳州三水人也。

translations.literal: Hou Junji was a man of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji was a native of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性矯飾，好矜誇，玩弓矢而不能成其藝，乃以武勇自稱。

translations.literal: By nature he was affected and pretentious, fond of boasting; he played with bow and arrow but could not master the skill, and so styled himself valiant in martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature affected and boastful, fond of showing off. He dabbled in archery without mastering it, and made his name instead on raw martial daring.

sentences.zh: 太宗在籓，引入幕府，數從征伐，累除左虞侯、車騎將軍，封全椒縣子。

translations.literal: When Taizong was still a prince, he brought Junji into his staff; Junji followed him on many campaigns and was repeatedly promoted to Left Cavalry Guard and Chariot-and-Cavalry General, enfeoffed as Baron of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Taizong was still Prince of Qin, he brought Hou Junji into his staff. Junji campaigned with him repeatedly and rose through the ranks to Left Cavalry Guard and Chariot-and-Cavalry General, receiving the title Baron of Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 漸蒙恩遇，參預謀議。

translations.literal: He gradually won favor and took part in strategic deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually won the prince's trust and was drawn into counsel on major decisions.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉之誅也，君集之策居多。

translations.literal: In the execution of Jiancheng and Yuanji, Junji's stratagems figured most largely.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji were killed, Hou Junji's plans had contributed more than anyone else's.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷左衛將軍，以功進封潞國公，賜邑千戶，尋拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Junji was made Left Guard General; for his merit he was advanced to Duke of Lu with a fief of a thousand households, and soon appointed Right Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong ascended the throne, Junji was appointed Left Guard General. For his service he was promoted to Duke of Lu with a fief of a thousand households, and soon afterward named Right Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，遷兵部尚書，參議朝政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of War and took part in deliberating court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 630 he was made Minister of War and joined the deliberations of state.

sentences.zh: 時將討吐谷渾伏允，命李靖為西海道行軍大總管，以君集及任城王道宗並為之副。

translations.literal: At that time an expedition against Fuyun of Tuyuhun was planned; Li Jing was appointed Grand Commander of the Western Sea Route Army, with Junji and Prince Daozong of Rencheng both as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to campaign against Fuyun of the Tuyuhun, Li Jing was named Grand Commander of the Western Sea Route Army, with Hou Junji and Prince Daozong of Rencheng as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，師次鄯州，君集言於靖曰：「大軍已至，賊虜尚未走險，宜簡精銳，長驅疾進，彼不我虞，必有大利。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year the army halted at Shan Prefecture; Junji said to Jing: "The main force has arrived, yet the enemy has not yet fled into defiles. We should select elite troops and drive swiftly forward—they will not expect us, and great gain is certain."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 635 the army reached Shan Prefecture. Junji told Li Jing, "Our main force is here, but the enemy has not yet retreated into the mountains. We should pick our best troops and strike at speed—they will not be on guard, and the advantage will be ours."

sentences.zh: 若此策不行，潛遁必遠，山障為阻，討之實難。

translations.literal: If this plan is not adopted, they will slip away to a great distance; mountain barriers will block us, and subduing them will be truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act on this plan, they will slip away deep into the wilds. The mountains will bar our path, and finishing them off will be far harder."

sentences.zh: 」靖然其計，乃簡精銳，輕齎深入。

translations.literal: " Jing approved his plan, selected elite troops, and with light baggage pressed deep in.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing agreed. He picked elite troops, traveled light, and drove deep into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 道宗追及伏允之眾於庫山，破之。

translations.literal: Daozong overtook Fuyun's forces at Mount Ku and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozong caught Fuyun's army at Mount Ku and routed it.

sentences.zh: 伏允輕兵入磧，以避官軍。

translations.literal: Fuyun led light troops into the desert to avoid the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun withdrew with a light force into the desert to evade the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 靖乃中分士馬為兩道併入，靖與薛萬均、李大亮趣北路，使侯君集、道宗趣南路。

translations.literal: Jing then divided troops and horses in two and advanced on both routes: he with Xue Wan Jun and Li Daliang took the northern road, while Hou Junji and Daozong were sent on the southern road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing then split his force in two. He took the northern route with Xue Wan Jun and Li Daliang, while Hou Junji and Prince Daozong marched south.

sentences.zh: 歷破邏真谷，逾漢哭山，經途二千餘里，行空虛之地。

translations.literal: They successively broke through Luozhen Valley and crossed Mount Han Ku; the route was more than two thousand li through empty land.
translations.idiomatic: They fought through Luozhen Valley, crossed Mount Han Ku, and marched more than two thousand li across barren country.

sentences.zh: 盛夏降霜，山多積雪，轉戰過星宿川，至於柏海，頻與虜遇，皆大克獲。

translations.literal: In midsummer frost fell; the mountains held deep snow. Fighting their way past the Star River and on to Cypress Sea, they met the enemy repeatedly and each time won great spoils.
translations.idiomatic: Frost fell in the height of summer; snow lay thick on the peaks. Fighting all the way past the Star River to Cypress Sea, they met the enemy again and again and each time carried off a great victory.

sentences.zh: 北望積玉山，觀河源之所出焉。

translations.literal: Looking north to Mount Jade Heap, they beheld where the Yellow River's source issues forth.
translations.idiomatic: They looked north toward Mount Jade Heap and saw where the Yellow River rises.

sentences.zh: 乃旋師，與李靖會於大非川，平吐谷渾而還。

translations.literal: They then turned the army about, joined Li Jing at the Great Fei River, pacified Tuyuhun, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then withdrew, joined Li Jing on the Great Fei River, pacified the Tuyuhun, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與長孫無忌等俱受世封，授君集陳州刺史，改封陳國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he and Zhangsun Wuji and others alike received hereditary enfeoffments; Junji was made Prefect of Chen and his title changed to Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In 637 he and Zhangsun Wuji and others received hereditary titles. Junji was appointed Prefect of Chen and raised to Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜吏部尚書，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 君集出自行伍，素無學術，及被任遇，方始讀書。

translations.literal: Junji had risen from the ranks and had no learning; only after he won appointment did he begin to study books.
translations.idiomatic: Junji had come up through the army and had no schooling. Only after he rose to high office did he take up reading.

sentences.zh: 典選舉，定考課，出為將領，入參朝政，並有時譽。

translations.literal: Whether administering selections, fixing performance reviews, going forth as a commander, or entering to take part in court policy, he won contemporary praise in each role.
translations.idiomatic: Whether he ran civil-service selections, set performance reviews, led troops in the field, or sat in on court policy, he earned a solid reputation at the time.

sentences.zh: 高昌王麹文泰時遏絕西域商賈，太宗徵文泰入朝，而稱疾不至，詔以君集為交河道行軍大總管討之。

translations.literal: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang had long blocked Western Regions merchants; Taizong summoned Wentai to court, but he pleaded illness and did not come. An edict made Junji Grand Commander of the Jiaohe Route Army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang had been cutting off trade from the Western Regions. Taizong summoned him to court, but Wentai pleaded illness and stayed away. The emperor ordered Hou Junji to lead the Jiaohe Route Army against him.

sentences.zh: 文泰聞王師將起，謂其國人曰：「唐國去此七千里，涉磧闊二千里，地無水草，冬風凍寒，夏風如焚。

translations.literal: When Wentai heard that the imperial army was about to march, he told his people: "Tang lies seven thousand li from here; crossing the desert is two thousand li wide; the land has no grass or water; winter winds freeze one stiff; summer winds burn like fire."
translations.idiomatic: When Wentai heard that a Tang army was coming, he told his people, "Tang is seven thousand li away. The desert crossing alone is two thousand li across—no grass, no water. Winter winds freeze you to the bone; summer winds scorch like flame."

sentences.zh: 風之所吹，行人多死，當行百人不能得至，安能致大軍乎？

translations.literal: Where the wind blows, travelers mostly die; of every hundred who set out, not one can arrive—how could they bring a great army here?
translations.idiomatic: Where those winds blow, travelers die in droves. Of every hundred who set out, scarcely one arrives. How could they march a great army here?"

sentences.zh: 若頓兵於吾城下，二十日食必盡，自然魚潰，乃接而虜之，何足憂也！

translations.literal: If they camp beneath our walls, in twenty days their food will be gone; they will naturally scatter like fish from a broken net, and we can take them as captives—what is there to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: If they camp under our walls, their provisions will be gone in twenty days. They will break apart on their own, and we can take them prisoner. What is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 」及軍至磧口，而文泰卒，其子智盛襲位。

translations.literal: " When the army reached the desert mouth, Wentai died and his son Zhicheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army reached the desert frontier, Wentai was dead and his son Zhicheng had taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 君集率兵至柳谷，候騎言文泰剋日將葬，國人咸集。

translations.literal: Junji led the army to Willow Valley; scouts reported that Wentai's burial was set for a fixed day and the whole nation would gather.
translations.idiomatic: Junji marched to Willow Valley. Scouts reported that Wentai's funeral was set for a fixed day and the whole kingdom would be gathered there.

sentences.zh: 諸將請襲之，君集曰：「不可，天子以高昌驕慢無禮，使吾恭行天罰，今襲人於墟墓之間，非問罪之師也。

translations.literal: The generals asked to strike them; Junji said: "It cannot be done. The Son of Heaven sent us because Gaochang was arrogant and rude, to carry out Heaven's punishment with due ceremony. To strike men amid ruins and graves is not an army that comes to demand account."
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged a surprise attack. Junji refused. "The Son of Heaven sent us because Gaochang was arrogant and insolent—to carry out Heaven's punishment with proper dignity. To strike them at a funeral among the tombs is not how a punitive army behaves."

sentences.zh: 」於是鼓行而前，攻其田地。

translations.literal: " He then advanced with drums beating and attacked their farmlands.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced with drums beating and attacked their farmland instead.

sentences.zh: 賊嬰城自守，君集諭之，不行。

translations.literal: The enemy clung to the walls in defense; Junji urged them to yield, but they would not.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shut themselves in the city. Junji called on them to surrender, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，大軍之發也，上召山東善為攻城器械者，悉遣從軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the great army set out, the emperor had summoned from east of the mountains all who were skilled at siege engines and sent them with the force.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army marched, the emperor had summoned from east of the mountains every man skilled in siege engines and sent them with the expedition.

sentences.zh: 君集遂刊木填隍，推撞車撞其睥睨，數丈頹穴，拋車石擊其城中，其所當者無不糜碎，或張氈被，用障拋石，城上守陴者不復得立。

translations.literal: Junji then felled timber to fill the moat, pushed battering rams against the parapets until several zhang of wall collapsed into holes, and used catapults to hurl stones into the city—whatever they struck was pulverized; some spread felt blankets to block the stones, yet defenders on the battlements could no longer stand.
translations.idiomatic: Junji felled trees to fill the moat and drove battering rams against the parapets until whole sections of wall—several yards high—crumbled away. Catapults hurled stones into the city; nothing they hit was left whole. Some defenders spread felt blankets to block the stones, but men on the battlements could no longer hold their posts.

sentences.zh: 遂拔之，虜其男女七千餘口，仍進兵圍其都城。

translations.literal: They then took it, capturing more than seven thousand men and women, and pressed on to besiege the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They took the city, captured more than seven thousand men and women, and marched on to besiege the capital.

sentences.zh: 智盛窮蹙，致書於君集曰：「有罪於天子者，先王也。

translations.literal: Zhicheng, hard pressed, sent a letter to Junji saying: "He who offended the Son of Heaven was my late father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng, cornered, wrote to Junji: "The one who offended the Son of Heaven was my late father.

sentences.zh: 天罰所加，身已喪背。

translations.literal: Heaven's punishment has fallen; his person is already dead and gone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's punishment has already struck him down—he is dead and gone.

sentences.zh: 智盛襲位未幾，不知所以愆闕，冀尚書哀憐。

translations.literal: Zhicheng has held the throne only a short while and does not know wherein he has failed; he hopes the Minister will show pity.
translations.idiomatic: I have only just succeeded him and do not know what fault you find in me. I beg your Excellency's mercy."

sentences.zh: 」君集報曰：「若能悔禍，宜束手軍門。

translations.literal: " Junji replied: "If you can repent your misfortune, you should bind your hands and come to the camp gate."
translations.idiomatic: Junji answered, "If you wish to repent, come to the camp gate with bound hands."

sentences.zh: 」智盛猶不出，因命士卒填其隍塹，發拋車以攻之。

translations.literal: Zhicheng still would not come out, so Junji ordered the soldiers to fill moat and ditch and brought catapults to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng still would not surrender. Junji ordered his men to fill the moat and opened the catapults on the city.

sentences.zh: 又為十丈高樓，俯視城內，有行人及飛石所中處，皆唱言之，人多入室避石。

translations.literal: He also built a tower ten zhang high to look down into the city; wherever there were people walking or wherever flying stones would strike, he had it called out, and many went indoors to avoid the stones.
translations.idiomatic: He built a tower ten zhang high to overlook the city. Spotters called out wherever anyone walked or wherever a stone would land, and most people fled indoors to escape the barrage.

sentences.zh: 初，文泰與西突厥欲谷設約，有兵至，共為表裡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wentai had agreed with Yugu She of the Western Turks that when troops came they would act as outer and inner allies.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai had earlier made a pact with Yugu She of the Western Turks: if an army came, they would strike from without while Gaochang struck from within.

sentences.zh: 及聞君集至，欲谷設懼而西走千餘里，智盛失援，計無所出，遂開門出降。

translations.literal: When he heard Junji had arrived, Yugu She in fear fled west more than a thousand li; Zhicheng lost his support, could devise no plan, and opened the gates to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Yugu She heard that Junji had arrived, he fled west in fear for more than a thousand li. Zhicheng lost his ally, saw no way out, and opened the gates to surrender.

sentences.zh: 君集分兵略地，遂平其國，俘智盛及其將吏，刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: Junji divided his forces to overrun the land, pacified the state, took Zhicheng and his commanders captive, carved stone to record the achievement, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Junji sent detachments to overrun the country, pacified the kingdom, took Zhicheng and his officers prisoner, carved a stone monument to record the victory, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 君集初破高昌，曾未奏請，輒配沒無罪人，又私取寶物。

translations.literal: When Junji had first taken Gaochang, he had not yet memorialized the throne but already assigned innocent people to penal servitude and privately took treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Right after taking Gaochang, Junji had not even reported to court yet when he began assigning innocent people to penal servitude and helping himself to valuables.

sentences.zh: 將士知之，亦競來盜竊，君集恐發其事，不敢制。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, knowing this, also rushed to steal; Junji feared exposure of the affair and did not dare restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men, seeing what he did, joined in the looting. Junji feared exposure and did not dare stop them.

sentences.zh: 及京師，有司請推其罪，詔下獄。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, the responsible offices asked to investigate his crimes, and an edict sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, the responsible offices moved to prosecute him, and an edict sent him to prison.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本以為，功臣大將不可輕加屈辱，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben held that meritorious great generals must not lightly be subjected to humiliation, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben argued that a meritorious commander must not be lightly humiliated, and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 君集等或位居輔佐，或職惟爪牙，並蒙拔擢，受將帥之任，不能正身奉法，以報陛下之恩。

translations.literal: Junji and the others, some holding posts as counselors, some serving only as talons and fangs, all were raised up by selection and received commanders' commissions, yet could not correct their persons and uphold the law to repay Your Majesty's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Junji and his fellows—some in high counsel, some your claws and fangs—were all raised up by Your Majesty and given command. They failed to conduct themselves lawfully and repay your grace.

sentences.zh: 舉措肆情，罪負盈積，實宜繩之刑典，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Their conduct was unrestrained; their guilt piled full—it is indeed fitting to bind them to the penal code and thereby rectify court order.
translations.idiomatic: Their conduct was reckless and their offenses numerous. By rights they should be bound to the penal code to restore discipline at court.

sentences.zh: 但高昌昏迷，人神共棄，在朝議者，以其地在遐荒，咸欲置之度外。

translations.literal: Yet Gaochang was benighted; men and spirits alike cast it off; those who deliberated at court, because its land lay in distant wilds, all wished to set it beyond concern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaochang was benighted—abandoned by men and spirits alike. At court many argued that because it lay in the far wilderness, the matter could be left alone.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下運獨見之明，授決勝之略，君集等奉行聖算，遂得指期平殄。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty deployed unique foresight and entrusted the strategy for certain victory; Junji and the others carried out the sage calculation and so were able to extinguish the foe within the appointed term.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty, with singular foresight, entrusted the strategy for victory. Junji and the others carried out your plan and destroyed the enemy within the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 若論事實，並是陛下之功，君集等有道路之勞，未足稱其勳力。

translations.literal: If one speaks of the facts, it was all Your Majesty's achievement; Junji and the others had only the toil of the road—not enough to be called meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: In truth the achievement was yours alone. Junji and the others had only the hardship of the march—hardly merit enough to boast of.

sentences.zh: 而陛下天德弗宰，乃推功於將帥。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty's heaven-sent virtue did not keep it, and you pushed the merit onto the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty, in heaven's own magnanimity, credited the commanders instead.

sentences.zh: 露布初至，便降大恩，從征之人，皆沾滌蕩。

translations.literal: When the victory bulletin first arrived, great grace was at once bestowed; all who had gone on the campaign were bathed in cleansing favor.
translations.idiomatic: The moment the victory bulletin arrived, you showered them with grace. Every man who had marched was washed clean of fault.

sentences.zh: 及其凱旋，特蒙曲宴，又對萬國，加之重賞。

translations.literal: When they returned in triumph they were specially granted a private banquet, and before all the realms heavy rewards were added.
translations.idiomatic: On their triumphant return you gave them a special banquet and, before all the realms, heaped on further rewards.

sentences.zh: 內外文武，咸欣陛下賞不逾時。

translations.literal: Civil and military within and without all rejoiced that Your Majesty's rewards did not miss their season.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials alike rejoiced that your rewards never came late.

sentences.zh: 而不經旬日，並付大理，雖乃君集等自掛網羅，而在朝之人未知所犯，恐海內又疑陛下唯錄其過，似遺其功。

translations.literal: Yet within not ten days they were all handed to the Court of Review; though Junji and the others had ensnared themselves, those at court did not know their offenses, and I fear the realm will again suspect Your Majesty records only their faults and seems to forget their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within ten days they were all handed to the Court of Review. Though Junji and the others had brought this on themselves, the court did not know their crimes. I fear the realm will suspect that you record only their faults and forget their service.

sentences.zh: 臣以下才，謬參近職，既有所見，不敢默然。

translations.literal: Your servant, with mean talent wrongly sharing a near post, having seen this, dares not keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of little talent who has been wrongly placed near your person. Having seen this, I dare not keep silent.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之人君，出師命將，克敵則獲重賞，不克則受嚴刑。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that ancient rulers, when sending armies and commissioning generals, gave heavy reward if the enemy was overcome and severe punishment if they were not.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that ancient rulers, when they sent armies abroad, rewarded commanders richly if they won and punished them harshly if they failed.

sentences.zh: 是以賞其有功也，雖貪殘淫縱，必蒙青紫之寵；

translations.literal: Thus when rewarding merit, even if greedy, cruel, and dissolute, one still received the purple and blue favor;
translations.idiomatic: When they rewarded merit, even the greedy, cruel, and dissolute still won the purple and blue of high office;

sentences.zh: 當其有罪也，雖勤躬潔己，不免鈇鉞之誅。

translations.literal: when they had guilt, even if diligent in person and pure in conduct, they did not escape execution by axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: when they were guilty, even the diligent and self-restrained did not escape the axe.

sentences.zh: 故《周書》曰：「記人之功，忘人之過，宜為君者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the 《Documents of Zhou》 says: "Record men's merit, forget men's faults—this is fitting for a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the 《Documents of Zhou》 says, "Record a man's merit and forget his faults—that is how a ruler should act."

sentences.zh: 」昔漢貳師將軍李廣利損五萬之師，糜億萬之費，經四年之勞，唯獲駿馬三十匹。

translations.literal: " In former times Han's General of the Ershi Li Guangli lost fifty thousand troops, squandered hundreds of millions in cost, and after four years' labor gained only thirty fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times General Li Guangli of the Ershi campaign lost fifty thousand men, spent hundreds of millions, and after four years of labor brought back only thirty fine horses.

sentences.zh: 雖斬宛王之首，而貪不愛卒，罪惡甚多。

translations.literal: Though he cut off the King of Dayuan's head, he was greedy and did not cherish his soldiers—his crimes were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Though he took the King of Dayuan's head, he was greedy and careless of his men. His crimes were many.

sentences.zh: 武帝為萬里征伐，不錄其過，遂封廣利海西侯，食邑八千戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, for the sake of campaigning ten thousand li, did not record his faults, and enfeoffed Guangli as Marquis of Haixi with a fief of eight thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign had reached ten thousand li, Emperor Wu overlooked his faults and enfeoffed Guangli as Marquis of Haixi with eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又校尉陳湯矯詔興師，雖斬郅支單于，而湯素貪盜，所收康居財物，事多不法，為司隸所繫。

translations.literal: Again, Commandant Chen Tang forged an edict to raise troops; though he beheaded Zhizhi Chanyu, Tang had always been greedy and thieving—the Kangju goods he took involved many unlawful acts, and the Director of Law Enforcement detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Chen Tang once forged an edict to raise troops. Though he killed Zhizhi Chanyu, Tang was habitually greedy. Much of the Kangju booty he seized was taken unlawfully, and the Director of Law Enforcement had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 湯乃上疏曰：「與吏士共誅郅支，幸得擒滅。

translations.literal: Tang then submitted a memorial saying: "Together with officers and soldiers I executed Zhizhi and by fortune captured and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang submitted a memorial: "Together with my officers and men I destroyed Zhizhi and was fortunate enough to capture and kill him.

sentences.zh: 今司隸乃收系案驗，是為郅支報仇也。

translations.literal: Now the Director of Law Enforcement detains and investigates me—this is avenging Zhizhi."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Director of Law Enforcement arrests and tries me—as if he were avenging Zhizhi."

sentences.zh: 」元帝赦其罪，封湯關內侯，賜黃金百斤。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan pardoned his crime, enfeoffed Tang as Marquis within the Passes, and bestowed a hundred jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan pardoned him, made him Marquis within the Passes, and gave him a hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 又晉龍驤將軍王浚有平吳之功，而王渾等論浚違詔，不受節度，軍人得孫皓寶物，並燒皓宮及船。

translations.literal: Again, Jin's Dragon-Charger General Wang Jun had the merit of pacifying Wu, yet Wang Hun and others charged that Jun had disobeyed the edict, refused command, and that his soldiers had taken Sun Hao's treasures and burned Hao's palace and ships.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Dragon-Charger General Wang Jun had conquered Wu, yet Wang Hun and others accused him of disobeying orders, refusing command, and letting his men seize Sun Hao's treasures and burn Hao's palace and ships.

sentences.zh: 浚上表曰：「今年平吳，誠為大慶，於臣之身，更為咎累。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial saying: "This year the pacification of Wu is truly a great celebration, but for your servant's person it is instead a burden of blame."
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote, "The conquest of Wu this year is a great celebration for the realm—but for me it has become a source of blame."

sentences.zh: 」武帝赦而不推，拜輔國大將軍，封襄陽侯，賜絹萬匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu pardoned him and did not pursue the matter, appointing him Supporting-the-State Grand General, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Xiangyang, and bestowing ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu pardoned him without further inquiry, made him Supporting-the-State Grand General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiangyang, and gave him ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 近隋新義郡公韓擒虎平陳之日，縱士卒暴亂叔寶宮內，文帝亦不問罪，雖不進爵，拜擒虎上柱國，賜物八千段。

translations.literal: Recently, when Sui's Duke of Xinyi Han Qinhu pacified Chen, he let his soldiers run riot in Chen Shubao's palace; Emperor Wen also did not inquire into guilt—though he did not advance his rank, he made Qinhu Supreme Pillar of State and bestowed eight thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: More recently, when Sui's Duke of Xinyi Han Qinhu took Chen, his men looted Chen Shubao's palace. Emperor Wen did not prosecute him either. He did not raise his rank, but made Qinhu Supreme Pillar of State and gave him eight thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 由斯觀之，將帥之臣，廉慎者寡，貪求者眾，是以黃石公《軍勢》曰：「使智，使勇，使貪，使愚。

translations.literal: From this one sees that among commanders, the incorrupt and cautious are few and the greedy seekers many; thus Master Yellow Stone's 《Military Momentum》 says: "Use the wise, use the brave, use the greedy, use the foolish."
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that among commanders the scrupulous are few and the grasping many. Master Yellow Stone wrote in 《Military Momentum》: "Use the wise, use the brave, use the greedy, use the foolish."

sentences.zh: 故智者樂立其功，勇者好行其志，貪者邀趨其利，愚者不計其死。

translations.literal: Thus the wise delight in establishing merit, the brave love to carry out their will, the greedy hurry after profit, and the foolish do not reckon with death."
translations.idiomatic: The wise delight in winning merit, the brave love to carry out their will, the greedy rush after gain, and the foolish do not count the cost of death."

sentences.zh: 」是知前聖莫不收人之長，棄人之短，良為此也。

translations.literal: " Hence former sages all took men's strengths and discarded men's weaknesses—truly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages of old always took men's strengths and set aside their weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞，夫天地之道，以覆載為先；

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the Way of Heaven and Earth puts covering and bearing first;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Heaven and Earth themselves put sheltering and sustaining first;

sentences.zh: 帝王之德，以含弘為美。

translations.literal: the virtue of emperors and kings takes inclusive magnanimity as its beauty.
translations.idiomatic: and the virtue of emperors and kings finds its beauty in inclusive magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 夫以區區漢武及歷代諸帝，猶能宥廣利等，況陛下天縱神武，振宏圖以定六合，豈獨正茲刑網，不行古人之事哉！

translations.literal: If even the narrow scope of Han Wu and the emperors of successive ages could pardon Guangli and the like, how much more Your Majesty, heaven-endowed and divinely martial, who has raised a great design to settle the six directions—would you alone tighten this penal net and not do what the ancients did!
translations.idiomatic: If even a ruler of Han Wu's measure and the emperors of every age could pardon men like Guangli, how much more should you, heaven-endowed and divinely martial, who have raised a great design to settle the realm—would you alone tighten the penal net and refuse what the ancients did!

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖懷，當自已有斟酌。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that in Your Sage's breast there must be deliberation of your own.
translations.idiomatic: I trust that Your Majesty's own heart will weigh the matter.

sentences.zh: 臣今所以陳聞，非敢私君集等，庶以螢爝末光，增暉日月。

translations.literal: Your servant now speaks forth not daring to favor Junji and the others privately, but hoping with the last gleam of a firefly or torch to add radiance to sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I speak now not to plead privately for Junji and his fellows, but in hope that this firefly's gleam may add a little light to sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 倘陛下降雨露之澤，收雷電之威，錄其微勞，忘其大過，使君集重升朝列，復預驅馳，雖非清貞之臣，猶是貪愚之將。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would send down the moisture of rain and dew and withhold the might of thunder and lightning, record their slight labors and forget their great faults, so that Junji might again ascend the court ranks and once more take part in driving forward—though not a pure and upright minister, still a greedy and foolish general.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would send down rain and dew instead of thunder and lightning, record their small service and forget their great faults, restore Junji to court and to the field again—he may not be an upright man, but he is still a useful greedy fool of a general.

sentences.zh: 斯則陛下聖德，雖屈法而德彌顯；

translations.literal: Then Your Majesty's sage virtue, though the law were bent, would shine all the brighter;
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty's sage virtue, though the law were bent, would shine all the brighter;

sentences.zh: 君集等愆過，雖蒙宥而過更彰。

translations.literal: Junji and the others' faults, though pardoned, would be displayed all the more clearly.
translations.idiomatic: and Junji and the others, though pardoned, would feel their faults all the more keenly.

sentences.zh: 足使立功之士，因茲而皆勸；

translations.literal: Enough to make all who would establish merit take heart from this;
translations.idiomatic: Men who would win merit would all take heart from it;

sentences.zh: 負罪之將，由斯而改節矣。

translations.literal: and guilty generals thereby reform their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: and guilty generals would reform their ways.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，乃釋。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Junji was released.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and Junji was released.

sentences.zh: 君集自以有功於西域，而以貪冒被囚，志殊怏怏。

translations.literal: Junji considered that he had merit in the Western Regions yet had been imprisoned for greed, and his spirit was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Junji believed he had earned merit in the Western Regions and resented bitterly that greed had landed him in prison.

sentences.zh: 十七年，張亮以太子詹事出為洛州都督，君集激怒亮曰：「何為見排？

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhang Liang, having served as the Crown Prince's Household Mentor, went out as Military Governor of Luo Prefecture; Junji in anger provoked Liang, saying: "Why am I being pushed aside?
translations.idiomatic: In 643 Zhang Liang left his post as the crown prince's household mentor to become military governor of Luo Prefecture. Junji confronted him angrily: "Why are you being pushed aside?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「是公見排，更欲誰冤！

translations.literal: " Liang said: "It is you who are being pushed aside—whom else would you blame!
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied, "It is you who are being pushed aside—whom else would you blame!"

sentences.zh: 」君集曰：「我平一國，還觸天子大嗔，何能抑排！

translations.literal: " Junji said: "I pacified a whole state and still provoked the Son of Heaven's great wrath—how could I be pushed down!
translations.idiomatic: Junji said, "I pacified an entire kingdom and still drew the Son of Heaven's wrath—how could I not be pushed aside!

sentences.zh: 」因攘袂曰：「鬱鬱不可活，公能反乎？

translations.literal: " He then flung back his sleeves and said: "I am so depressed I cannot live—can you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: He flung back his sleeves and said, "Life is unbearable like this—will you rebel with me?

sentences.zh: 當與公反耳。

translations.literal: I will rebel with you."
translations.idiomatic: I will rebel with you."

sentences.zh: 」亮密以聞，太宗謂亮曰：「卿與君集俱是功臣，君集獨以語卿，無人聞見，若以屬吏，君集必言無此。

translations.literal: " Liang secretly reported it; Taizong told Liang: "You and Junji are both meritorious ministers; Junji spoke of this only to you, with no witness. If handed to the judicial officers, Junji will certainly say it never happened.
translations.idiomatic: Liang reported this in secret. Taizong told him, "You and Junji are both meritorious ministers. He spoke of this only to you, with no witness. If we hand it to the judicial officers, Junji will deny it.

sentences.zh: 兩人相證，事未可知。

translations.literal: With only the two of you testifying against each other, the matter cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: With only the two of you testifying against each other, the truth cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢其事，待君集如初。

translations.literal: " He then shelved the matter and treated Junji as before.
translations.idiomatic: He set the matter aside and treated Junji as before.

sentences.zh: 尋與諸功臣同畫像於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was painted in portrait together with the other meritorious ministers in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his portrait was painted with those of the other meritorious ministers in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時庶人承乾在東宮，恐有廢立，又知君集怨望，遂與通謀。

translations.literal: At that time the deposed commoner Chengqian was in the Eastern Palace, fearing deposition and replacement; knowing Junji's resentment, he entered into conspiracy with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the deposed crown prince Chengqian, fearing he would be replaced, knew of Junji's resentment and entered into conspiracy with him.

sentences.zh: 君集子婿賀蘭楚石時為東宮千牛，承乾令數引君集入內，問以自安之術。

translations.literal: Junji's son-in-law Helan Chushi then served as Eastern Palace Thousand-Bull; Chengqian had him repeatedly bring Junji inside and ask him for means to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Junji's son-in-law Helan Chushi served as a palace guard in the Eastern Palace. Chengqian had him bring Junji in repeatedly to ask how he might secure his position.

sentences.zh: 君集以承乾劣弱，意欲乘釁以圖之，遂贊承乾陰圖不軌，嘗舉手謂承乾曰：「此好手，當為用之。

translations.literal: Junji, considering Chengqian weak and inferior, intended to seize an opening to plot against him; he urged Chengqian in secret toward unlawful designs and once raised his hand and told Chengqian: "These are good hands—they should be put to use."
translations.idiomatic: Junji saw that Chengqian was weak and meant to exploit the chance. He encouraged the prince's secret plots and once held up his hands, saying, "These are capable hands—you should use them."

sentences.zh: 」君集或慮謀洩，心不自安，每中夜蹶然而起，嘆咤久之。

translations.literal: " Junji sometimes feared the plot would leak; his heart was ill at ease, and each midnight he would start up from sleep and sigh and exclaim for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Junji sometimes feared the plot would leak. Uneasy in his heart, he would start up at midnight and sigh for a long while.

sentences.zh: 其妻怪而謂之曰：「公，國之大臣，何為乃爾？

translations.literal: His wife, wondering, said to him: "You are a great minister of the state—why act like this?
translations.idiomatic: His wife, puzzled, said to him, "You are a great minister of the state—why are you like this?

sentences.zh: 必當有故。

translations.literal: There must be a reason.
translations.idiomatic: There must be a reason.

sentences.zh: 若有不善之事，孤負國家，宜自歸罪，首領可全。

translations.literal: If there is some evil affair, having failed the state, you should confess guilt yourself—your head may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: If you have done wrong against the state, confess yourself—your life may be spared."

sentences.zh: 」君集不能用。

translations.literal: " Junji would not follow her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Junji would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及承乾事發，君集被收，楚石又詣闕告其事。

translations.literal: When Chengqian's affair broke open, Junji was arrested, and Chushi again went to the palace gates to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqian's plot was exposed, Junji was arrested, and Chushi went to court to report the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨問曰：「我不欲令刀筆吏辱公，故自鞫驗耳。

translations.literal: Taizong came in person to question him, saying: "I did not wish to let clerks humiliate you, and so I examine the case myself."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong questioned him in person. "I did not want clerks to humiliate you," he said, "so I am examining this myself."

sentences.zh: 」君集辭窮。

translations.literal: " Junji had no further words.
translations.idiomatic: Junji had nothing left to say.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂百僚曰：「往者家國未安，君集實展其力，不忍置之於法。

translations.literal: Taizong told the hundred officials: "In former days when house and state were not yet secure, Junji truly displayed his strength; I could not bear to subject him to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told the officials, "When the realm was still unsettled, Junji truly served with all his strength. I could not bear to punish him then.

sentences.zh: 我將乞其性命，公卿其許我乎？

translations.literal: I will beg his life—will you ministers grant me this?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to beg his life—will you grant it?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣爭進曰：「君集之罪，天地所不容，請誅之以明大法。

translations.literal: " The ministers pressed forward together, saying: "Junji's crime is what Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate—we beg that he be executed to clarify the great law."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed forward as one. "Junji's crime is intolerable to Heaven and Earth," they said. "Execute him to uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 」太宗謂君集曰：「與公長訣矣，而今而後，但見公遺像耳！

translations.literal: " Taizong told Junji: "I take long farewell of you; from now on I shall see only your surviving portrait!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told Junji, "We take our long farewell. From now on I shall see only your portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion!"

sentences.zh: 」因歔欷下泣。

translations.literal: " He then sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 遂斬於四達之衢，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Junji was then beheaded at the crossroads where four ways meet, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded at the public crossroads, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 君集臨刑，容色不改，謂監刑將軍曰：「君集豈反者乎，蹉跌至此！

translations.literal: Facing execution, Junji's countenance did not change; he told the supervising general: "Was Junji truly a rebel? A stumble brought me here!
translations.idiomatic: At the block Junji's face did not change. He told the supervising general, "Was I truly a rebel? A stumble brought me here!

sentences.zh: 然嘗為將，破滅二國，頗有微功。

translations.literal: Yet I once served as a general and destroyed two states—there is some slight merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I once commanded armies and destroyed two kingdoms. I have some small merit.

sentences.zh: 為言於陛下，乞令一子以守祭祀。

translations.literal: Speak to His Majesty for me and beg that one son be allowed to maintain the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Tell His Majesty for me: let one son remain to tend the ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 」由是特原其妻及一子，徙於嶺南。

translations.literal: For this his wife and one son were specially spared and exiled to the lands south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: For this his wife and one son were specially spared and exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 張亮，鄭州滎陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang was a man of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 素寒賤，以農為業。

translations.literal: He had always been poor and lowly, and made his living by farming.
translations.idiomatic: He came from a poor farming family.

sentences.zh: 倜儻有大節，外惇厚而內懷詭詐，人莫之知。

translations.literal: Unconventional and possessed of great resolve, outwardly sincere and thick yet inwardly harboring deceit—no one knew it.
translations.idiomatic: He was unconventional and bold in spirit, outwardly honest and inwardly cunning, and no one saw through him.

sentences.zh: 大業末，李密略地滎、汴，亮杖策從之，未被任用。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign Li Mi seized the lands of Xing and Bian; Liang followed him with staff in hand but was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, when Li Mi seized Xing and Bian, Liang joined him but won no post.

sentences.zh: 屬軍中有謀反者，亮告之，密以為至誠，署驃騎將軍，隸於徐勣。

translations.literal: When there was a rebel plot in the army, Liang reported it; Mi considered him utterly sincere and appointed him Cavalry General, subordinate to Xu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When a plot formed in the army, Liang reported it. Li Mi took him for utterly loyal, made him Cavalry General, and placed him under Xu Ji.

sentences.zh: 及勣以黎陽歸國，亮頗贊成其事，乃授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ji brought Liyang over to the Tang, Liang greatly supported the affair and was made Prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Ji surrendered Liyang to Tang, Liang strongly backed the move and was made Prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 會王世充陷鄭州，亮不得之官，孤軍無援，遂亡命於共城山澤。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong then took Zheng Prefecture; Liang could not reach his post, his isolated army had no aid, and he fled into the mountains and marshes of Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong then seized Zheng. Liang could not take office, his isolated force had no support, and he fled into the wilds around Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 後房玄齡、李勣以亮倜儻有智謀，薦之於太宗，引為秦府車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later Fang Xuanling and Li Ji, because Liang was unconventional and possessed stratagems, recommended him to Taizong, who brought him in as Chariot-and-Cavalry General of the Prince of Qin's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fang Xuanling and Li Ji recommended him to the future Taizong as a man of bold wit, and he was made Chariot-and-Cavalry General on the Prince of Qin's staff.

sentences.zh: 漸蒙顧遇，委以心膂。

translations.literal: He gradually won favor and was entrusted as backbone and sinew.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually won trust and was treated as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 會建成、元吉將起難，太宗以洛州形勝之地，一朝有變，將出保之。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng and Yuanji were about to raise trouble, Taizong, because Luoyang was a strategically superior place, planned that if trouble came in a morning he would go out to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji were about to strike, Taizong saw that Luoyang was a strategic stronghold and planned to withdraw there if crisis came.

sentences.zh: 遣亮之洛陽，統左右王保等千餘人，陰引山東豪傑以俟變，多出金帛，恣其所用。

translations.literal: He sent Liang to Luoyang to command Wang Bao and more than a thousand men of the Left and Right, secretly drawing in powerful men east of the mountains to await change, dispensing much gold and silk for them to use as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liang to Luoyang with Wang Bao and more than a thousand men, secretly recruiting powerful families east of the mountains and lavishing gold and silk on them as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 元吉告亮欲圖不軌，坐是屬吏，亮卒無所言。

translations.literal: Yuanji reported that Liang intended unlawful designs; for this he was handed to judicial officers, yet Liang in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanji accused Liang of plotting treason. He was handed to the judicial officers but said nothing in his defense.

sentences.zh: 事釋，遣還洛陽。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared he was sent back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was cleared, he was sent back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及建成死，授懷州總管，封長平郡公。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng died, Liang was made Commander of Huai Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jiancheng's death, Liang was made commander of Huai Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，歷遷御史大夫，轉光祿卿，進封鄅國公，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was transferred through Censor-in-Chief to Minister of Splendid Happiness, advanced to Duke of Yi with a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 631 he rose through Censor-in-Chief to Minister of Splendid Happiness, was raised to Duke of Yi, and received a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後歷豳、夏、鄜三州都督。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Military Governor of Bin, Xia, and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as military governor of Bin, Xia, and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 七年，魏王泰為相州都督而不之部，進亮金紫光祿大夫，行相州大都督長史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Tai of Wei was Military Governor of Xiang but did not go to his post; Liang was advanced to Golden Purple-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acted as Chief Administrator of the Xiang Grand Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In 633 Prince Tai of Wei was named military governor of Xiang but never took up the post. Liang was promoted to Golden Purple-Gleam Grand Master and served as acting chief administrator of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改封鄖國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year his title was changed to Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In 637 his title was changed to Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 亮所蒞之職，潛遣左右伺察善惡，發扌適奸隱，動若有神，抑豪強而恤貧弱，故所在見稱。

translations.literal: In every post Liang held he secretly sent attendants to observe good and evil, exposing hidden wrongdoing as if moved by a spirit; he checked the powerful and comforted the poor and weak, and so wherever he went he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held, Liang secretly sent agents to watch for wrongdoing, exposed hidden crimes as if by divine insight, checked the powerful, and helped the poor—wherever he served he won praise.

sentences.zh: 初，亮之在州也，棄其本妻，更娶李氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang was in the prefectures, he abandoned his original wife and took Lady Li in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the provinces he abandoned his first wife and married Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 李素有淫行，驕妒特甚，亮寵憚之。

translations.literal: Lady Li had always been licentious, proud and jealous in the extreme; Liang both favored and feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was notoriously licentious, proud, and fiercely jealous. Liang both doted on her and feared her.

sentences.zh: 後至相州，有鄴縣小兒，以賣筆為業，善歌舞，李見而悅之，遂與私通。

translations.literal: Later at Xiang Prefecture there was a youth of Ye County who sold brushes for a living and was skilled at song and dance; Lady Li saw him and was pleased, and had a secret affair with him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiang there was a boy from Ye County who sold brushes and sang well. Lady Li took a liking to him and began an affair.

sentences.zh: 假言亮先與其母野合所生，收為亮子，名曰慎幾。

translations.literal: She falsely said Liang had earlier had illicit union with the boy's mother in the wilds and fathered him; she took him as Liang's son and named him Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed the boy was Liang's illegitimate son by the youth's mother, adopted him, and named him Shenji.

sentences.zh: 亮前婦子慎微，每以養慎幾致諫，亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang's son by his former wife, Shenwei, repeatedly remonstrated over raising Shenji; Liang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's son by his first wife, Shenwei, repeatedly urged him not to keep Shenji, but Liang refused.

sentences.zh: 李尤好左道，所至巫覡盈門，又干預政事，由是亮之聲稱漸損。

translations.literal: Lady Li especially favored heterodox ways; wherever they went shamans and diviners filled the gates, and she also meddled in government affairs—thus Liang's reputation gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was devoted to sorcery; shamans thronged their house wherever they went, and she meddled in affairs of state. Liang's reputation steadily fell.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 640 he was again made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太子詹事，出為洛州都督。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Household Mentor of the Heir Apparent and went out as Military Governor of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became the crown prince's household mentor and was sent out as military governor of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及侯君集誅，以亮先奏其將反，優詔褒美，遷刑部尚書，參預朝政。

translations.literal: When Hou Junji was executed, because Liang had earlier reported that Junji would rebel, a gracious edict praised him; he was made Minister of Justice and took part in court policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Junji was executed, Liang was rewarded with a gracious edict for having reported Junji's treasonous talk. He was made Minister of Justice and joined court deliberations.

sentences.zh: 太宗將伐高麗，亮頻諫不納，因自請行。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to attack Goguryeo, Liang repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded, and then asked to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to attack Goguryeo, Liang remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then volunteered to go himself.

sentences.zh: 以亮為滄海道行軍大總管，管率舟師。

translations.literal: Liang was made Grand Commander of the Canghai Route Army in charge of the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was named Grand Commander of the Canghai Route Army to lead the fleet.

sentences.zh: 自東萊渡海，襲沙卑城，破之，俘男女數千口。

translations.literal: Crossing the sea from Donglai, he raided Shabei city, took it, and captured several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed from Donglai, stormed Shabei, and took several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 進兵頓於建安城下，營壘未固，士卒多樵牧。

translations.literal: Advancing, he halted beneath Jian'an city; the camps were not yet secure and many soldiers were out gathering firewood and grazing.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and camped below Jian'an. The fortifications were not yet secure, and many men were out gathering wood and grazing.

sentences.zh: 賊眾奄至，軍中惶駭。

translations.literal: The enemy force suddenly arrived and the army was seized with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck suddenly and panic spread through the camp.

sentences.zh: 亮素怯懦，無計策，但踞胡床，直視而無所言，將士見之，翻以亮為有膽氣。

translations.literal: Liang had always been timid and had no stratagem; he only sat on a barbarian camp-stool, staring straight ahead and saying nothing—the soldiers, seeing this, instead took Liang to have nerve.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was by nature timid and had no plan. He simply sat on his camp stool, staring ahead in silence. The soldiers, seeing this, took his stillness for courage.

sentences.zh: 其副總管張金樹等乃鳴鼓令士眾擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: His deputy commander Zhang Jinshu and others then beat the drums and ordered the troops to strike the enemy, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Zhang Jinshu beat the drums, ordered the men to attack, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 太宗知其無將帥材而不之責。

translations.literal: Taizong knew he lacked the talent of a commander and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew he lacked commander's talent and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 有方術人程公穎者，亮親信之。

translations.literal: There was a man of occult arts, Cheng Gongying, whom Liang trusted intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Liang placed great trust in a practitioner of occult arts named Cheng Gongying.

sentences.zh: 初，在相州，陰召公穎謂曰：「相州形勝之地，人言不出數年有王者起，公以為何如？

translations.literal: Earlier, at Xiang Prefecture, he secretly summoned Gongying and said: "Xiang is a strategically superior place; people say that within a few years a king will arise—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: At Xiang he once summoned Gongying in secret and said, "Xiang is a strategic place. People say a king will rise here within a few years. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」公穎知其有異志，因言亮臥似龍形，必當大貴。

translations.literal: " Gongying, knowing he had rebellious intent, therefore said that when Liang lay down he resembled a dragon's form and would surely attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Gongying sensed his rebellious intent and told him that when he slept he resembled a dragon and was destined for greatness.

sentences.zh: 又有公孫常者，頗擅文辭，自言有黃白之術，尤與亮善。

translations.literal: There was also Gongsun Chang, quite skilled in literary phrasing, who claimed to possess the art of transmuting base metals to gold and silver, and was especially close to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Gongsun Chang, a man of letters who claimed to know the art of making gold and silver, and he was especially close to Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮謂曰：「吾嘗聞圖讖『有弓長之君當別都』，雖有此言，實不願聞之。

translations.literal: Liang said to him: "I once heard in prognostic texts, 'A lord Zhang-Chang will establish a separate capital'—though such words exist, I truly do not wish to hear them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang told him, "I once heard a prophecy: 'A lord Zhang will set up a separate capital.' Such words exist, but I do not wish to hear them."

sentences.zh: 」常又言亮名應圖錄，亮大悅。

translations.literal: " Chang also said Liang's name matched the charts and records; Liang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chang also said Liang's name matched the prophecies. Liang was delighted.

sentences.zh: 二十年，有陝人常德玄告其事，並言亮有義兒五百人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year a man of Shan, Chang Deyuan, reported the affair and also said Liang had five hundred sworn sons.
translations.idiomatic: In 646 a man from Shan named Chang Deyuan reported the plot and said Liang had five hundred sworn sons.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣法官按之，公穎及常證其罪，亮曰：「此二人畏死見誣耳。

translations.literal: Taizong sent judicial officers to investigate; Gongying and Chang testified to his guilt; Liang said: "These two men, fearing death, bear false witness.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent investigators. Gongying and Chang testified against him. Liang said, "These two fear death and lie about me.

sentences.zh: 」又自陳佐命之舊，冀有寬貸。

translations.literal: " He also declared his old service in founding the dynasty, hoping for lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his old service in founding the dynasty, hoping for mercy.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「亮有義兒五百，畜養此輩，將何為也？

translations.literal: Taizong told his attendants: "Liang has five hundred sworn sons—raising such men, for what purpose?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his attendants, "Liang has five hundred sworn sons. What does he keep them for?

sentences.zh: 正欲反耳。

translations.literal: He means to rebel, nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: To rebel, of course."

sentences.zh: 」命百僚議其獄，多言亮當誅，唯將作少匠李道裕言亮反形未具，明其無罪。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to deliberate the case; most said Liang should be executed, but only Assistant Director of Imperial Construction Li Daoyu said the signs of rebellion were not yet complete and made clear he was guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the officials to deliberate. Most said Liang should die. Only Assistant Director of Imperial Construction Li Daoyu argued that the evidence of rebellion was incomplete and that Liang was innocent.

sentences.zh: 太宗既盛怒，竟斬於市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Taizong, already in great anger, had him beheaded in the market after all and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, furious, had him beheaded in the market and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，刑部侍郎有闕，令執政者妙擇其人，累奏皆不可。

translations.literal: More than a year later the post of Vice Minister of Justice was vacant; the chief ministers were told to choose the man with care, but repeated nominations were all rejected.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the post of Vice Minister of Justice fell vacant. The chief ministers nominated candidate after candidate, but none satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕得其人也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I have found the man.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I have found the man.

sentences.zh: 往者李道裕議張亮雲『反形未具』，此言當矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Daoyu argued over Zhang Liang that 'the signs of rebellion were not yet complete'—those words were right.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Daoyu said of Zhang Liang that 'the signs of rebellion were not yet complete,' he was right.

sentences.zh: 雖不即從，至今追悔。

translations.literal: Though I did not follow him at once, to this day I regret it.
translations.idiomatic: I did not heed him then, and I regret it to this day."

sentences.zh: 」遂授道裕刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Daoyu Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Daoyu Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 薛萬徹，雍州咸陽人，自燉煌徙焉。

translations.literal: Xue Wanche was a man of Xianyang in Yong Prefecture, his family having moved there from Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanche was a native of Xianyang in Yong Prefecture; his family had moved there from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 隋左御衛大將軍世雄子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of Sui's Left Imperial Guard Grand General Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Sui's Left Imperial Guard Grand General Xue Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 世雄大業末卒於涿郡太守。

translations.literal: Shixiong died at the end of Daye while serving as Prefect of Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong died at the end of the Sui while serving as prefect of Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 萬徹少與兄萬均隨父在幽州，俱以武略為羅藝所親待。

translations.literal: Wanche in youth followed his elder brother Wanjun with their father in You Prefecture; both, for their martial stratagems, were favored and treated kindly by Luo Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Wanche and his elder brother Wanjun followed their father in You Prefecture. Both won favor from Luo Yi for their martial skill.

sentences.zh: 尋與藝歸附高祖，授萬均上柱國、永安郡公，萬徹車騎將軍、武安縣公。

translations.literal: Soon they followed Yi in submitting to Gaozu; Wanjun was made Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an, Wanche Chariot-and-Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Yi submitted to Gaozu, Wanjun was made Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an, and Wanche Chariot-and-Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 會竇建德率眾十萬來寇范陽，藝逆拒之。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande led a hundred thousand men to raid Fanyang, Yi met them in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande led a hundred thousand men against Fanyang, Luo Yi met him in battle.

sentences.zh: 萬均謂藝曰：「眾寡不敵，今若出門，百戰百敗，當以計取之。

translations.literal: Wanjun told Yi: "Few against many—we cannot match them; if we go out now we will lose a hundred battles in a hundred fights. We must take them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjun told Luo Yi, "We are too few to match them. If we march out we will lose every fight. We must use stratagem.

sentences.zh: 可令羸兵弱馬阻水背城為陣以誘之，觀賊之勢，必渡水交兵。

translations.literal: We can set weak soldiers and poor horses with their backs to the water and the city in formation to lure them; watching the enemy's momentum, they will surely cross the water to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Post weak troops and poor horses with the water at their backs and the city behind them to lure the enemy. They will surely cross the river to fight.

sentences.zh: 萬均請精騎百人伏於城側，待其半渡擊之，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: Wanjun asks for a hundred elite horsemen hidden beside the city; when the enemy is half across, strike them—the foe will surely be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Give me a hundred elite horsemen hidden beside the city. When they are half across the river, strike them—the enemy will surely break."

sentences.zh: 」藝從其言。

translations.literal: " Yi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 建德果引軍渡水，萬均邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Jiande indeed led his army across the water; Wanjun intercepted and struck, routing them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande crossed as predicted. Wanjun ambushed him and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 明年，建德率眾二十萬復攻幽州，賊已攀堞，萬均與萬徹率敢死士百人從地道而出，直掩賊背擊之，賊遂潰走。

translations.literal: The next year Jiande led two hundred thousand men to attack You again; the enemy had already scaled the battlements when Wanjun and Wanche led a hundred dare-to-die men out through a tunnel, struck straight at the enemy's rear, and the foe then broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jiande returned with two hundred thousand men. The enemy had already scaled the walls when Wanjun and Wanche led a hundred dare-to-die men through a tunnel, struck their rear, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 及太宗平劉黑闥，引萬均為右二護軍，恩顧甚至。

translations.literal: When Taizong pacified Liu Heita, he brought Wanjun in as Right Second Guard General and favored him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong defeated Liu Heita, he made Wanjun Right Second Guard General and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成又引萬徹置於左右。

translations.literal: The Hidden Heir Jiancheng also brought Wanche in to keep at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Li Jiancheng also kept Wanche at his side.

sentences.zh: 建成被誅，萬徹率宮兵戰於玄武門，鼓噪欲入秦府，將士大懼。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng was executed, Wanche led palace troops to fight at Xuanwu Gate, beating drums and shouting as if to enter the Prince of Qin's residence; the officers and soldiers were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng was killed, Wanche led palace troops to fight at Xuanwu Gate, drumming and shouting as if to storm the Prince of Qin's residence. Taizong's men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 及梟建成首示之，萬徹與數十騎亡於終南山。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng's head was displayed on a pole, Wanche fled with several dozen horsemen into the Zhongnan Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng's head was displayed, Wanche fled with several dozen horsemen into the Zhongnan Mountains.

sentences.zh: 太宗累遣使諭意，萬徹釋仗而來。

translations.literal: Taizong repeatedly sent envoys to explain his intent; Wanche laid down his weapons and came in.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent envoys again and again to reassure him. Wanche laid down his arms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其忠於所事，不之罪也。

translations.literal: Taizong, because he had been loyal to whom he served, did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong spared him because he had been loyal to his master.

sentences.zh: 萬均，貞觀初歷遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: Wanjun, at the beginning of Zhenguan, was transferred through posts to Vice Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan, Wanjun rose to Vice Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 柴紹之擊梁師都，以萬徹為副。

translations.literal: When Chai Shao attacked Liang Shidu, Wanche was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Chai Shao attacked Liang Shidu, Wanche served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 未至朔方數十里，突厥四面而至，官軍稍卻。

translations.literal: Before reaching within several tens of li of Shuofang, Turks came from all four sides and the imperial army fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Still several tens of li from Shuofang, Turks closed in from every side and the Tang force fell back.

sentences.zh: 萬均與萬徹橫出擊之，斬其驍將，虜陣亂，因而乘之，殺傷被野。

translations.literal: Wanjun and Wanche struck out across the field, beheaded their fierce general, the barbarian formation was thrown into disorder, and pressing the advantage they killed and wounded until the plain was covered.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjun and Wanche charged out, killed the enemy's best general, threw their formation into disorder, and pressed the attack until the field was strewn with dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 鼓行而進，遂圍師都。

translations.literal: Advancing with drums beating, they then besieged Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced with drums beating and besieged Shidu.

sentences.zh: 俄而師都見殺，城降，突厥不敢來援。

translations.literal: Before long Shidu was killed, the city surrendered, and the Turks did not dare come to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shidu was killed, the city surrendered, and the Turks did not dare intervene.

sentences.zh: 萬徹後從李靖擊突厥頡利可汗於塞北，以功授統軍，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Wanche later followed Li Jing in striking the Turkic Khan Jieli in the northern marches; for merit he was made Army Commander and advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche later followed Li Jing against the Turkic Khan Jieli in the northern marches and was made Army Commander and Duke of a commandery for his service.

sentences.zh: 初，靖將擊吐谷渾，請萬徹同行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing was about to strike Tuyuhun, he asked Wanche to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing prepared to campaign against the Tuyuhun, he asked Wanche to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及至賊境，與諸將各率百餘騎先行，卒與虜數千騎相遇。

translations.literal: When they reached the enemy territory, he and the other generals each led a hundred-odd horsemen ahead, and suddenly met several thousand barbarian horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching enemy country he and the other generals each led a little over a hundred horsemen ahead and suddenly ran into several thousand enemy cavalry.

sentences.zh: 萬徹單騎馳擊之，虜無敢當者。

translations.literal: Wanche charged alone to strike them; none of the barbarians dared stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche charged alone into them; no enemy dared stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 還謂諸將曰：「賊易與耳！

translations.literal: Returning, he told the generals: "The enemy are easy opponents!
translations.idiomatic: He rode back and told the other generals, "These enemies are nothing!

sentences.zh: 」躍馬復進，諸將隨之，斬數千級，人馬流血，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: " He spurred his horse forward again, the generals followed, and they cut down several thousand; men and horses bled—their valor topped all three armies.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse forward again, the others followed, and they cut down thousands. Men and horses ran with blood. His courage topped the whole army.

sentences.zh: 又與萬均破吐谷渾天柱王於赤水源，獲其雜畜二十萬計，追至河源。

translations.literal: Again with Wanjun he defeated Tuyuhun's King Tianzhu at Red Water Source, took on the order of two hundred thousand mixed livestock, and pursued to the River's source.
translations.idiomatic: With Wanjun he defeated the Tuyuhun King Tianzhu at Red Water Source, seized some two hundred thousand head of livestock, and pursued to the Yellow River's source.

sentences.zh: 萬均此後官至左屯衛大將軍，累封潞國公而卒。

translations.literal: Wanjun afterward rose to Left Encampment Guard Grand General, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjun later became Left Encampment Guard Grand General, was repeatedly raised to Duke of Lu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 萬徹尋丁母憂解職，俄起為右衛將軍，出為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Wanche soon left office for his mother's mourning, but was quickly recalled as Right Guard General and went out as Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche soon left office to mourn his mother, but was quickly recalled as Right Guard General and sent out as prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 會薛延陀率回紇、同羅之眾渡磧，南擊李思摩，萬徹副李勣援之。

translations.literal: When Xueyantuo led the peoples of the Uyghurs and Tongluo across the desert to strike Li Simo in the south, Wanche served as Li Ji's deputy in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyantuo led Uyghur and Tongluo forces across the desert to attack Li Simo in the south, Wanche served under Li Ji as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 與虜相遇，率數百騎為先鋒，擊其陣後，騎皆散，賊顧見，遂大潰。

translations.literal: Meeting the barbarians, he led several hundred horsemen as vanguard, struck their rear, their riders all scattered; the enemy looked back and saw, and then broke in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When they met the enemy, he led several hundred horsemen as vanguard, struck their rear, and scattered their riders. The enemy looked back, panicked, and broke completely.

sentences.zh: 追奔數十里，斬首三千餘級，獲馬萬五千匹。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout for several tens of li, they cut off more than three thousand heads and took fifteen thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued for miles, took more than three thousand heads, and captured fifteen thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 以功別封一子為縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of a county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as a county marquis.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授左衛將軍，尚丹陽公主，拜附馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was made Left Guard General, married Princess Danyang, and appointed Chief Commandant Escort.
translations.idiomatic: In 644 he was made Left Guard General, married Princess Danyang, and was appointed chief commandant escort.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右衛大將軍，轉杭州刺史，遷代州都督，復召拜右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Guard Grand General, then Prefect of Hangzhou, then Military Governor of Dai, and was again summoned as Right Martial Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Right Guard Grand General, then prefect of Hangzhou, then military governor of Dai, and was recalled as Right Martial Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 太宗從容謂從臣曰：「當今名將，唯李勣、道宗、萬徹三人而已。

translations.literal: Taizong at ease told his attending ministers: "Among famous generals today there are only Li Ji, Daozong, and Wanche."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told his ministers at leisure, "Among the famous generals of our day there are only three: Li Ji, Prince Daozong, and Xue Wanche."

sentences.zh: 李勣、道宗不能大勝，亦不大敗；

translations.literal: Li Ji and Daozong cannot win great victories, yet they do not suffer great defeats either;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji and Daozong do not win crushing victories, but they do not suffer crushing defeats either;

sentences.zh: 萬徹非大勝，即大敗。

translations.literal: Wanche, if not winning greatly, then loses greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Wanche either wins a crushing victory or suffers a crushing defeat."

sentences.zh: 」太宗嘗召司徒長孫無忌等十餘人宴於丹霄殿，各賜以貘皮，萬徹預焉。

translations.literal: Taizong once summoned Chancellor Zhangsun Wuji and more than ten others to feast in the Cinnabar Cloud Hall, each bestowing tapir hides; Wanche was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once summoned Chancellor Zhangsun Wuji and more than ten others to a feast in the Cinnabar Cloud Hall and gave each of them tapir hides. Wanche was among them.

sentences.zh: 太宗意在賜萬徹，而誤呼萬均，因愴然曰：「萬均朕之勳舊，不幸早亡，不覺呼名，豈其魂靈慾朕之賜也。

translations.literal: Taizong meant to bestow on Wanche but mistakenly called Wanjun's name; he therefore said in grief: "Wanjun was my old meritorious companion, who unhappily died young—I called his name without thinking; could his spirit desire my gift?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong meant to call Wanche but accidentally said Wanjun's name. Stricken, he said, "Wanjun was an old companion in merit who died too young. I called his name without thinking—does his spirit want this gift?"

sentences.zh: 」因令取貘皮，呼萬均以同賜而焚之於前，侍坐者無不感嘆。

translations.literal: " He then had the tapir hide taken, called Wanjun's name to bestow it likewise, and burned it before them; none of those seated in attendance failed to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: He had the hide brought forward, called Wanjun's name as if to give it to him, and burned it before the company. Everyone present was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，萬徹又為青丘道行軍大總管，率甲士三萬自萊州泛海伐高麗，入鴨綠水百餘里，至泊灼城，高麗震懼，多棄城而遁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Wanche was again Grand Commander of the Qingqiu Route Army, leading thirty thousand armored men from Laizhou across the sea to attack Goguryeo; they entered the Yalu more than a hundred li and reached Bojok city; Goguryeo was shaken with fear and many abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In 648 Wanche again led the Qingqiu Route Army, taking thirty thousand armored men from Laizhou by sea against Goguryeo. They entered the Yalu more than a hundred li and reached Bojok. Goguryeo was terrified and many towns were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 泊灼城主所夫孫率步騎萬餘人拒戰，萬徹遣右衛將軍裴行方領步卒為支軍繼進，萬徹及諸軍乘之，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Bojok's lord Suofusun led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to resist; Wanche sent Right Guard General Pei Xingfang to lead foot soldiers as a supporting army following up; Wanche and the other forces pressed them and the enemy broke in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Bojok, Suofusun, led more than ten thousand men to resist. Wanche sent Right Guard General Pei Xingfang with infantry as a follow-up force, then pressed the attack with the main army and routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 追奔百餘里，於陣斬所夫孫，進兵圍泊灼城。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout for more than a hundred li, they cut down Suofusun in the battle line and advanced to besiege Bojok.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued for more than a hundred li, killed Suofusun in battle, and advanced to besiege Bojok.

sentences.zh: 其城因山設險，阻鴨綠水以為固，攻之未拔。

translations.literal: The city relied on mountains for its defenses and used the Yalu as its bulwark; they attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The city used the mountains for defense and the Yalu as its moat. They attacked but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣將高文率烏骨、安地諸城兵三萬餘人來援，分置兩陣。

translations.literal: Goguryeo sent the general Gao Wen leading more than thirty thousand troops from the cities of Wugu and Andi in relief, arrayed in two formations.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo sent General Gao Wen with more than thirty thousand men from Wugu, Andi, and other cities in two formations.

sentences.zh: 萬徹分軍以當之，鋒刃才接而賊大潰。

translations.literal: Wanche divided his army to meet them; blades had scarcely crossed when the enemy broke in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche divided his force to meet them. Blades had barely crossed when the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 萬徹在軍，仗氣凌物，人或奏之。

translations.literal: Wanche in the army relied on his spirit to look down on others; some reported him to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Wanche bullied others with his temper, and some reported him to court.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，太宗謂曰：「上書者論卿與諸將不協，朕錄功棄過，不罪卿也。

translations.literal: When he came to audience, Taizong said: "Those who memorialized say you are not in harmony with the other generals. I record merit and set aside faults—I do not blame you."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience, Taizong said, "Memorials say you quarrel with the other generals. I record your merit and overlook your faults. I will not punish you."

sentences.zh: 」因取書焚之。

translations.literal: He then took the memorial and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: He took the memorial and burned it.

sentences.zh: 尋為副將、右衛將軍裴行方言其怨望，於是廷驗之，萬徹辭屈。

translations.literal: Soon his deputy, Right Guard General Pei Xingfang, spoke of his resentment; thereupon the matter was tried at court, and Wanche's words failed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his deputy Pei Xingfang accused him of disloyal talk. The case was tried at court and Wanche could not defend himself.

sentences.zh: 英國公李勣進曰：「萬徹職乃將軍，親惟主婿，發言怨望，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Duke of Ying Li Ji advanced and said: "Wanche's office is general, his kinship that of the ruler's son-in-law—yet he spoke with resentment; his crime brooks no sparing from execution."
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Ying Li Ji said, "Wanche is a general and the emperor's son-in-law. To speak with resentment is a crime that cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」因除名徙邊，會赦得還。

translations.literal: He was therefore struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier; when an amnesty came he was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls and exiled to the frontier. An amnesty later allowed him to return.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，授寧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was made Prefect of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In 651 he was appointed prefect of Ning.

sentences.zh: 入朝與房遺愛款暱，因謂遺愛曰：「今雖患腳，坐置京師，諸輩猶不敢動。

translations.literal: Coming to court he grew intimate with Fang Yiai and therefore told Yiai: "Though I now suffer in the feet, if seated in the capital the rest still would not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: At court he grew close to Fang Yiai and told him, "Even with my bad leg, if I sit in the capital the others still will not dare move."

sentences.zh: 」遺愛謂萬徹曰：「公若國家有變，我當與公立荊王元景為主。

translations.literal: " Yiai told Wanche: "If the state has a change, I will with you set up Prince Jing Yuanjing as ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Yiai told Wanche, "If the state falls into crisis, I will join you in making Prince Jing Yuanjing ruler."

sentences.zh: 」及謀洩，吏逮之，萬徹不之伏，遺愛證之，遂伏誅。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked, officers seized him; Wanche would not confess, but Yiai testified against him, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, officers arrested him. Wanche would not confess until Yiai testified against him. He was executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑大言曰：「薛萬徹大健兒，留為國家效死力固好，豈得坐房遺愛殺之乎！

translations.literal: Facing execution he cried out: "Xue Wanche is a great stalwart—fine to keep him to die for the state; how can he be killed because of Fang Yiai!
