translations.idiomatic: At the block he shouted, "Xue Wanche is a great fighting man! It would be fine to keep me to die for the state. How can I be killed because of Fang Yiai!"

sentences.zh: 」遂解衣謂監刑者疾斫。

translations.literal: " He then stripped and told the supervising executioner to strike quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped to the waist and told the executioner to strike quickly.

sentences.zh: 執刃者斬之不殊，萬徹叱之曰：「何不加力！

translations.literal: The blade-wielder struck but did not sever him; Wanche shouted at him: "Why not use more force!
translations.idiomatic: The executioner's blow did not kill him. Wanche shouted, "Strike harder!

sentences.zh: 」三斫乃絕。

translations.literal: " Three strokes were needed before he died.
translations.idiomatic: It took three strokes to finish him.

sentences.zh: 萬徹長兄萬淑，亦有戰功。

translations.literal: Wanche's elder brother Wanshu also had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche's elder brother Wanshu also won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，至營州都督，檢校東夷校尉，封梁郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he rose to Military Governor of Ying Prefecture, Acting Commandant of the Eastern Barbarians, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became military governor of Ying, acting commandant of the eastern barbarians, and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 季弟萬備，有孝行，母終，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Wanbei had filial conduct; when their mother died he built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Wanbei was famously filial. When their mother died he built a mourning hut beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 太宗降璽書弔慰，仍旌表其門。

translations.literal: Taizong sent down an imperial letter of condolence and also marked his gate with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent an imperial letter of condolence and marked his gate with official commendation.

sentences.zh: 後官至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he rose to Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 並先萬徹卒。

translations.literal: All died before Wanche.
translations.idiomatic: All three died before Wanche.

sentences.zh: 初，武德、貞觀之際，有盛彥師、盧祖尚、劉世讓、劉蘭、李君羨等，並有功名而不終其位。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Wude and Zhenguan periods, there were Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, Li Junxian, and others—all had merit and fame yet did not finish their offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude and Zhenguan periods there were also Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, and Li Junxian—men who won merit and fame but did not end their careers in honor.

sentences.zh: 盛彥師者，宋州虞城人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yanshi was a man of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yanshi was a native of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為澄城長。

translations.literal: During Daye he was magistrate of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui he served as magistrate of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 義師至汾陰，率賓客千餘人濟河上謁，拜銀青光祿大夫、行軍總管，從平京城。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Fenyin, he led more than a thousand retainers across the river to pay homage, was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Campaigning General, and followed in pacifying the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang army reached Fenyin, he led more than a thousand retainers across the river to submit. He was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master and campaigning general and helped take the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄與史萬寶鎮宜陽以拒東寇。

translations.literal: Soon he and Shi Wanbao garrisoned Yiyang to resist the eastern invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Shi Wanbao garrisoned Yiyang against the eastern rebels.

sentences.zh: 及李密之叛，將出山南，史萬寶懼密威名，不敢拒，謂彥師曰：「李密，驍賊也，又輔以王伯當，決策而叛，其下兵士思欲東歸，若非計出萬全，則不為也。

translations.literal: When Li Mi rebelled and was about to come out south of the mountains, Shi Wanbao feared Mi's fierce reputation and did not dare resist; he told Yanshi: "Li Mi is a ferocious bandit, aided moreover by Wang Bodang; having decided on rebellion, his soldiers below all wish to return east—unless the plan is utterly sure, it will not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi rebelled and prepared to march south of the mountains, Shi Wanbao feared his reputation and would not fight. He told Yanshi, "Li Mi is a ferocious enemy, aided by Wang Bodang. His men are desperate to get home east. Unless our plan is foolproof, we should not fight."

sentences.zh: 兵在死地，殆不可當。

translations.literal: Troops in dead ground are scarcely to be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Men with their backs to the wall are almost impossible to stop."

sentences.zh: 」彥師笑曰：「請以數千之眾邀之，必梟其首。

translations.literal: Yanshi laughed and said: "Allow me with several thousand men to intercept him—I will surely take his head."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi laughed. "Give me a few thousand men to ambush him, and I will take his head."

sentences.zh: 」萬寶曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: Wanbao said: "What plan will you use?"
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao asked, "What is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「軍法尚詐，不可為公說之。

translations.literal: He answered: "Military law favors deception—I cannot tell it to you."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Military law favors deception. I cannot tell you the plan."

sentences.zh: 」便領眾逾熊耳山南，傍道而止，令弓弩者夾路乘高，刀楯者伏於溪谷。

translations.literal: He then led his force over the southern slopes of Bear-Ear Mountain, halted beside the road, ordered archers to line the heights on both sides of the path, and sword-and-shield men to lie hidden in stream valleys.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men over the southern slopes of Bear-Ear Mountain and halted beside the road. Archers lined the heights on both sides; sword-and-shield men hid in the stream valleys.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「待賊半渡，一時齊發，弓弩據高縱射，刀楯即亂出薄之。

translations.literal: His order was: "When the enemy are half across, all fire at once; archers from the heights shoot freely, sword-and-shield men rush out in disorder to press them."
translations.idiomatic: His order ran: "When the enemy are half across, fire together. Archers shoot from the heights; sword-and-shield men rush out and close on them."

sentences.zh: 」或問之曰：「聞李密欲向洛州，而公入山，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked him: "I hear Li Mi intends to go toward Luo Prefecture—yet you enter the mountains; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "I hear Li Mi is heading for Luo Prefecture. Why are you going into the mountains?"

sentences.zh: 」彥師曰：「密聲言往洛，實走襄城就張善相耳，必當出人不意。

translations.literal: Yanshi said: "Mi says aloud he goes to Luo, but in truth he goes to Xiangcheng to join Zhang Shanxiang—he is sure to move where men do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi said, "Mi says he is going to Luo, but he is really heading for Xiangcheng to join Zhang Shanxiang. He will take an unexpected route.

sentences.zh: 若賊入谷口，我自後追之，山路險隘，無所展力，一夫殿後，必不能制。

translations.literal: If the bandits enter the mouth of the valley and I pursue from behind, the mountain road is narrow and steep and there is nowhere to deploy strength—a single man guarding the rear cannot be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If they enter the valley and I pursue from behind, the narrow mountain road gives no room to fight. One man guarding the rear could hold us off.

sentences.zh: 今吾先得入谷，擒之必矣。

translations.literal: Now if I enter the valley first, I am sure to capture them."
translations.idiomatic: If I enter the valley first, I am sure to take them."

sentences.zh: 」李密既度陝州，以為余不足慮，遂擁眾徐行，果逾山南渡。

translations.literal: Li Mi, having crossed Shan Prefecture, thought the remainder not worth concern and therefore led his host slowly; indeed they crossed south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi crossed Shan Prefecture, thinking nothing remained to fear him, and marched slowly. He crossed south of the mountains as Yanshi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 彥師擊之，密眾首尾斷絕，不得相救，遂斬李密，追擒伯當。

translations.literal: Yanshi struck them; Mi's host was cut off head from tail and could not aid one another; he then beheaded Li Mi and pursued and captured Bodang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi struck. Mi's force was cut in two and could not rescue itself. Yanshi killed Li Mi and captured Wang Bodang in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 以功封葛國公，拜武衛將軍，仍鎮熊州。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ge, made Martial Guard General, and still garrisoned Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ge, made Martial Guard General, and continued to garrison Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗討王世充，遣彥師與萬寶軍於伊闕，絕其山南之路。

translations.literal: When Taizong attacked Wang Shichong, he sent Yanshi and Wanbao to encamp at Yique and cut off the routes south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong attacked Wang Shichong, he sent Yanshi and Wanbao to Yique to cut Shichong's routes south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除宋州總管。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was made Commander of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, he was made commander of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，彥師之入關也，王世充以其將陳寶遇為宋州刺史，處其家不以禮，及此，彥師因事殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanshi entered the passes, Wang Shichong had his general Chen Baoyu as Prefect of Song and treated Yanshi's household without courtesy; now Yanshi seized an occasion to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshi had first entered the passes, Wang Shichong's general Chen Baoyu was prefect of Song and had treated Yanshi's family discourteously. Now Yanshi seized a pretext and killed him.

sentences.zh: 平生所惡數十家亦皆殺之。

translations.literal: Several tens of families he had hated all his life were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed several dozen families he had hated all his life.

sentences.zh: 州中震駭，重足而立。

translations.literal: The prefecture was shaken with terror; men stood as if on overlapping feet.
translations.idiomatic: The whole prefecture was terrified. People walked on tiptoe in fear.

sentences.zh: 會徐圓朗反，彥師為安撫大使，因戰，遂沒於賊。

translations.literal: When Xu Yuanlang rebelled, Yanshi was Pacification Commissioner; in battle he was then lost to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Yuanlang rebelled, Yanshi was sent as pacification commissioner, was defeated in battle, and fell into enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 圓朗禮厚之，令彥師作書報其弟，令舉城降己。

translations.literal: Yuanlang treated him with thick courtesy and had Yanshi write a letter to his younger brother telling him to surrender the city to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang treated him well and made him write to his younger brother urging the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 彥師為書曰：「吾奉使無狀，被賊所擒，為臣不忠，誓之以死。

translations.literal: Yanshi wrote the letter: "I on mission behaved badly and was seized by bandits; as a minister I am disloyal and swear it with death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi wrote, "I failed in my mission and was captured by rebels. As a minister I am disloyal and swear to die for it.

sentences.zh: 汝宜善侍老母，勿以吾為念。

translations.literal: You should well serve our old mother—do not think of me."
translations.idiomatic: Serve our mother well. Do not think of me."

sentences.zh: 」圓朗初色動，而彥師自若，圓朗乃笑曰：「盛將軍乃有壯節，不可殺也。

translations.literal: Yuanlang at first changed color, but Yanshi was composed; Yuanlang then laughed and said: "General Sheng has a stalwart integrity—he cannot be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang's face fell at first, but Yanshi remained calm. Yuanlang laughed and said, "General Sheng has true steel in him. He cannot be killed."

sentences.zh: 」待之如舊。

translations.literal: He treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 賊平，彥師竟以罪賜死。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Yanshi in the end was granted death for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, Yanshi was nevertheless sentenced to death for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 盧祖尚者，字季良，光州樂安人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zushang, style Jiliang, was a man of Le'an in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zushang, courtesy name Jiliang, was a native of Le'an in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父禧，隋虎賁郎將。

translations.literal: His father Xi was a Sui Tiger-Gallop Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi had been a Sui Tiger-Gallop commandant.

sentences.zh: 累葉豪富，傾財散施，甚得人心。

translations.literal: For generations the family had been wealthy; he poured out wealth in distribution and won men's hearts greatly.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had been wealthy. He gave freely and won great loyalty.

sentences.zh: 大業末，召募壯士逐捕群盜。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he recruited stalwarts to pursue and capture bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he recruited stalwarts to hunt down bandit gangs.

sentences.zh: 時年甚少，而武力過人，又御眾嚴整，所向有功。

translations.literal: Though very young at the time, his martial strength surpassed others, and he also commanded troops with stern order—wherever he went there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Though very young, he was exceptionally strong and commanded his men with strict discipline. Wherever he went he won success.

sentences.zh: 群盜畏憚，不敢入境。

translations.literal: The bandit gangs feared and respected him and did not dare enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits feared him and did not dare enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 及宇文化及作亂，州人請祖尚為刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji made rebellion, the people of the prefecture asked Zushang to be prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, the people of the prefecture asked Zushang to become their prefect.

sentences.zh: 祖尚時年十九，升壇歃血，以誓其眾，泣涕歔欷，悲不自勝，眾皆感激。

translations.literal: Zushang was then nineteen; he ascended the altar and drank the blood oath to pledge his host, weeping and sobbing, grief beyond bearing—all were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zushang was only nineteen. He mounted the altar, swore an oath in blood before his followers, and wept until he could not speak. All were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 王世充立越王侗，祖尚遣使從之，侗授祖尚光州總管。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong set up Prince Yue of Tong; Zushang sent envoys to follow him, and Tong appointed Zushang Military Governor of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong set up Prince Yue of Tong, Zushang submitted to him and was made military governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 及世充自立，遂舉州歸款，高祖嘉之，賜璽書勞勉，拜光州刺史，封弋陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Shichong declared himself ruler, Zushang then offered the whole prefecture in submission; Gaozu praised him, bestowed an imperial letter of encouragement, made him Prefect of Guang, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong declared himself emperor, Zushang surrendered the whole prefecture to Tang. Gaozu praised him, sent an imperial letter of encouragement, made him prefect of Guang, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，從趙郡王孝恭討輔公礻石，為前軍總管，攻其宣、歙州，克之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude he followed Prince Xiaogong of Zhao in attacking Fu Gongshi, served as Vanguard Army Commander, attacked his Xuan and She prefectures, and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In 623 he followed Prince Xiaogong of Zhao against Fu Gongshi as vanguard commander, attacked Xuan and She, and took them.

sentences.zh: 進擊賊帥馮惠亮、陳正通，並破之。

translations.literal: Advancing, he struck the bandit chiefs Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong and defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the rebel leaders Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong and defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功授蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, for merit he was made Prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, he was made prefect of Jiang for his service.

sentences.zh: 又歷壽州都督、瀛州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: He also served in succession as Military Governor of Shou and Prefect of Ying, winning a name for ability in each.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as military governor of Shou and prefect of Ying, earning a reputation for competence in each post.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，交州都督、遂安公壽以貪冒得罪，太宗思求良牧，朝臣咸言祖尚才兼文武，廉平正直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan the Military Governor of Jiao, Duke of Sui'an Shou, was punished for greed; Taizong sought a good governor, and the court ministers all said Zushang combined civil and martial talent and was incorrupt, fair, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan the military governor of Jiao, Duke Shou of Sui'an, was punished for corruption. Taizong sought a worthy governor, and the ministers all praised Zushang as talented in both civil and military affairs, honest and upright.

sentences.zh: 征至京師，臨朝謂之曰：「交州大籓，去京甚遠，須賢牧撫之。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, Taizong told him at court: "Jiao is a great frontier, very far from the capital—it needs a worthy governor to comfort it.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, Taizong told him, "Jiao is a great frontier region, far from the capital. It needs a worthy governor.

sentences.zh: 前後都督皆不稱職，卿有安邊之略，為我鎮邊，勿以道遠為辭也。

translations.literal: Former and later governors have all been unfit for office; you have a plan to secure the frontier—secure the border for me, and do not decline because the road is far."
translations.idiomatic: Your predecessors have all failed. You have the skill to secure the frontier. Go and govern it for me. Do not refuse because it is far away."

sentences.zh: 」祖尚拜謝而出，既而悔之，以舊疾為辭。

translations.literal: Zushang bowed in thanks and left, but afterward regretted it and pleaded an old illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zushang bowed, thanked him, and left—but afterward regretted it and pleaded an old illness.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣杜如晦諭旨，祖尚固辭。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Du Ruhui to convey the imperial intent; Zushang firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Du Ruhui to explain the order again. Zushang still refused.

sentences.zh: 又遣其妻兄周范往諭之曰：「匹夫相許，猶須存信。

translations.literal: He again sent his wife's brother Zhou Fan to explain, saying: "When common men make promises to one another, they must keep faith.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zushang's brother-in-law Zhou Fan to reason with him: "Even common men keep their promises.

sentences.zh: 卿面許朕，豈得後方悔之？

translations.literal: You promised me to my face—how can you afterward regret it?
translations.idiomatic: You promised the emperor to his face. How can you regret it now?

sentences.zh: 宜可早行，三年必自相召，卿勿推拒，朕不食言。

translations.literal: You should go soon; in three years you will surely be recalled—do not refuse; I do not break my word."
translations.idiomatic: Go at once. In three years you will be recalled. Do not refuse. The emperor does not break his word."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「嶺南瘴癘，皆日飲酒，臣不便酒，去無還理。

translations.literal: He answered: "South of the ranges there is miasma; all drink wine daily—I cannot drink wine; if I go there is no logic of return."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "South of the ranges the miasma is deadly and everyone drinks wine every day. I cannot drink wine. If I go, I will not come back."

sentences.zh: 」太宗大怒曰：「我使人不從，何以為天下命！

translations.literal: Taizong in great anger said: "If my orders are not obeyed, how can I command the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong flew into a rage. "If my orders are not obeyed, how can I command the realm!

sentences.zh: 」斬之於朝，時年三十餘。

translations.literal: " He had him beheaded at court; he was then a little over thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded at court. Zushang was a little over thirty.

sentences.zh: 尋悔之，使復其官廕。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and had Zushang's official privileges restored to his heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and restored official privileges to Zushang's heirs.

sentences.zh: 劉世讓，字元欽，雍州醴泉人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shirang, style Yuanqin, was a man of Liquan in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shirang, courtesy name Yuanqin, was a native of Liquan in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋征仕郎。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a Recruitment Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as a recruitment gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖入長安，世讓以湋川歸國，拜通議大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, Shirang offered Weichuan to the state and was made General Consultant for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, Shirang surrendered Weichuan and was made general consultant for discussion.

sentences.zh: 時唐弼餘黨寇扶風，世讓自請安輯，許之，俄得數千人。

translations.literal: At that time the remnant followers of Tang Bi raided Fufeng; Shirang asked on his own to pacify them, was permitted, and soon gained several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bi's remnant followers were raiding Fufeng. Shirang volunteered to pacify them, was approved, and soon gathered several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 復為安定道行軍總管，率兵以拒薛舉，戰敗，世讓及弟寶俱為舉軍所獲。

translations.literal: Again made Campaigning General of the Anding Route, he led troops to resist Xue Ju, was defeated, and Shirang and his younger brother Bao were both taken by Ju's army.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made campaigning general of the Anding route and led troops against Xue Ju. Defeated in battle, he and his brother Bao were both captured.

sentences.zh: 舉將至城下，令紿說城中曰：「大軍五道已趣長安，宜開門早降。

translations.literal: Ju was about to reach the walls and ordered Shirang to deceive the city, saying: "Five armies have already hastened toward Chang'an—you should open the gates and surrender early.
translations.idiomatic: As Ju approached the city he ordered Shirang to deceive the defenders: "Five armies are already marching on Chang'an. Open the gates and surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 」世讓偽許之，因告城中曰：「賊兵多少，極於此矣。

translations.literal: " Shirang falsely agreed, then told the city: "However many the bandit soldiers are, this is the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Shirang pretended to agree, then told the city, "This is all the enemy has. Hold firm.

sentences.zh: 宜善自固，以圖安全。

translations.literal: You should secure yourselves well to seek safety."
translations.idiomatic: Secure yourselves and you will be safe."

sentences.zh: 」舉重其執節，竟不之害。

translations.literal: Ju valued his holding to principle and in the end did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju respected his integrity and did not harm him.

sentences.zh: 太宗時屯兵高墌，世讓潛遣寶逃歸，言賊中虛實；

translations.literal: Taizong was then encamped at Gaoping; Shirang secretly sent Bao to escape and return, reporting the enemy's true and false strength;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was encamped at Gaoping. Shirang secretly sent Bao to escape and report the enemy's true strength;

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，賜其家帛千匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised him and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk on his household.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him and gave his family a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，得歸，授彭州刺史。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he returned and was made Prefect of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated he returned and was made prefect of Peng.

sentences.zh: 尋領陝東道行軍總管，與永安王孝基擊呂崇茂於夏縣，諸軍敗績，世讓與唐儉俱為賊所獲。

translations.literal: Soon he led the Shandong Route Army as Campaigning General, and with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji attacked Lü Chongmao at Xia County; the armies were defeated and Shirang and Tang Jian were both taken by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led the Shandong route army with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia County. The armies were defeated and Shirang and Tang Jian were captured.

sentences.zh: 獄中聞獨孤懷恩有逆謀，逃還以告高祖。

translations.literal: In prison he heard that Dugu Huai'en had a treasonous plot; he escaped and returned to tell Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he learned that Dugu Huai'en was plotting treason. He escaped and warned Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 時高祖方濟河，將幸懷恩之營，聞難驚曰：「劉世讓之至，豈非天命哉！

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was just crossing the river and about to visit Huai'en's camp; hearing of the peril he exclaimed in alarm: "Liu Shirang's arrival—is this not Heaven's command!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was crossing the river to visit Huai'en's camp. Hearing the warning he cried, "Liu Shirang's arrival—surely this is Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 」因勞之曰：「卿往陷薛舉，遣弟潛效款誠，今復冒危告難，是皆憂國忘身也。

translations.literal: " He then comforted him, saying: "You formerly fell into Xue Ju's hands and sent your brother in secret to show sincere intent; now again you braved danger to report peril—all this is caring for the state and forgetting the self."
translations.idiomatic: He praised him: "You were captured by Xue Ju and sent your brother in secret to serve the state. Now you risked your life again to warn us. This is true loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」尋封弘農郡公，賜莊一區、錢百萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong and given one estate and a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong and given an estate and a million in cash.

sentences.zh: 累轉并州總管，統兵屯於雁門。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Commander of Bing Prefecture and commanded troops garrisoned at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of Bing Prefecture and garrisoned troops at Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 突厥處羅可汗與高開道、苑君璋合眾，攻之甚急。

translations.literal: The Turkic Khan Chuluo joined forces with Gao Kaidao and Yuan Junzhang and attacked him fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Khan Chuluo joined Gao Kaidao and Yuan Junzhang and attacked him fiercely.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿鄭元璹先使在蕃，可汗令元璹來說之，世讓厲聲曰：「大丈夫奈何為夷狄作說客耶！

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuansui had earlier been sent among the barbarians; the Khan ordered Yuansui to come and persuade him; Shirang said in a harsh voice: "How can a great man act as a lobbyist for the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuansui had been sent to the Turks. The khan ordered him to persuade Shirang to surrender. Shirang thundered, "How can a true man serve as a lobbyist for barbarians!

sentences.zh: 」經日餘，虜乃退。

translations.literal: " After more than a day the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a day the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及元璹還，述世讓忠貞勇干，高祖下制褒美之，錫以良馬。

translations.literal: When Yuansui returned he reported Shirang's loyalty, steadfastness, courage, and capability; Gaozu issued an edict praising him and bestowed fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuansui returned he reported Shirang's loyalty and courage. Gaozu issued an edict praising him and gave him fine horses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召拜廣州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and made Commander of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and made commander of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將之任，高祖問以備邊之策，世讓答曰：「突厥南寇，徒以馬邑為其中路耳。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up the post, Gaozu asked him for a frontier-defense plan; Shirang answered: "The Turks raid south only because Mayi is their middle route.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office Gaozu asked his plan for defending the frontier. Shirang answered, "The Turks raid south only because Mayi is their main route.

sentences.zh: 如臣所計，請於崞城置一智勇之將，多儲金帛，有來降者厚賞賜之，數出奇兵略其城下，芟踐禾稼，敗其生業。

translations.literal: By my plan, place at Guo city a general wise and brave, store much gold and silk, richly reward those who come to surrender, repeatedly send odd troops to raid beneath their walls, cut and trample the grain, and ruin their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: By my plan, post a wise and brave general at Guo city with ample gold and silk. Reward deserters richly. Send raiding parties repeatedly to cut their grain and destroy their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 不出歲餘，彼當無食，馬邑不足圖也。

translations.literal: Within not a year they will have no food, and Mayi will not be worth plotting over."
translations.idiomatic: Within a year they will run out of food, and Mayi will no longer be worth their trouble."

sentences.zh: 」高祖無可任者，乃使馳驛往經略之。

translations.literal: Gaozu had no one he could appoint and therefore sent him by urgent relay to carry out the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had no one else to appoint and sent him by urgent relay to carry out the plan himself.

sentences.zh: 突厥懼其威名，乃縱反間，言世讓與可汗通謀，將為亂。

translations.literal: The Turks feared his fierce reputation and therefore spread a counter-plot, saying Shirang was in secret conspiracy with the Khan and would make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks feared his reputation and spread a rumor that Shirang was conspiring with the khan to rebel.

sentences.zh: 高祖不之察，遂誅世讓，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not investigate and therefore executed Shirang and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu did not investigate and had Shirang executed. His property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，突厥來降者言世讓初無逆謀，始原其妻子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Turks who came to surrender said Shirang had had no treasonous plot from the first, and only then were his wife and children pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan surrendered Turks said Shirang had never plotted treason. Only then were his wife and children pardoned.

sentences.zh: 劉蘭，字文郁，青州北海人也。

translations.literal: Liu Lan, style Wenyü, was a man of Beihai in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan, courtesy name Wenyü, was a native of Beihai in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋鄱陽郡書佐。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a clerical assistant in Poyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as a clerical assistant in Poyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 頗涉經史，善言成敗。

translations.literal: He had dipped considerably into the classics and histories and was skilled at speaking of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: He had read widely in the classics and histories and was skilled at analyzing success and failure.

sentences.zh: 然性多凶狡，見隋末將亂，交通不逞。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was much given to ferocity and cunning; seeing the end of Sui about to fall into chaos, he associated with unruly men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature fierce and cunning. Seeing the Sui about to collapse, he associated with outlaws.

sentences.zh: 於時北海完富，蘭利其子女玉帛，與群盜相應，破其本鄉城邑。

translations.literal: At that time Beihai was intact and wealthy; Lan coveted its sons and daughters, jade, and silk, responded to bandit gangs, and broke the cities of his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Beihai was then intact and wealthy. Lan coveted its people and wealth, joined with bandits, and sacked the cities of his home district.

sentences.zh: 武德中，淮安王神通為山東道安撫大使，蘭率宗黨往歸之。

translations.literal: During Wude, Prince Huai'an Shentong was Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Route; Lan led his clan and kin to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, Prince Huai'an Shentong was pacification commissioner for the Shandong route. Lan led his clan to submit to him.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷尚書員外郎。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he rose to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，梁師都尚據朔方，蘭上言攻取之計。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Liang Shidu still held Shuofang; Lan submitted a memorial with a plan to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, when Liang Shidu still held Shuofang, Lan submitted a plan to capture him.

sentences.zh: 太宗善之，命為夏州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: Taizong approved it and appointed him Military Administrator of the Xia Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and made him military administrator of Xia.

sentences.zh: 時梁師都以突厥之師頓於城下，蘭偃旗臥鼓，不與之爭鋒，賊徒宵遁，蘭追擊破之，遂進軍夏州。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Shidu with Turkic troops halted beneath the walls; Lan lowered banners and stilled drums and did not contend with them; the bandits fled by night; Lan pursued and defeated them, then advanced on Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu camped Turkic troops below the walls. Lan lowered his banners and drums and refused battle. The enemy fled by night. Lan pursued, routed them, and advanced on Xia.

sentences.zh: 及師都平，以功遷豐州刺史，征為右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Shidu was pacified, for merit he was transferred to Prefect of Feng and summoned as Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: When Shidu was defeated, Lan was made prefect of Feng for his service and summoned as Right Army General.

sentences.zh: 十一年，幸洛陽，以蜀王愔為夏州都督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Taizong visited Luoyang and made Prince Shu of Shu Military Governor of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In 637 Taizong visited Luoyang and made Prince Shu of Shu military governor of Xia.

sentences.zh: 愔不之籓，以蘭為長史，總其府事。

translations.literal: Shu did not go to his fief; Lan was made Chief Administrator and oversaw the princely establishment's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince never took up his post. Lan was made chief administrator and ran the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 時突厥攜離，有郁射設阿史那摸末率其部落入居河南。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks were divided; Yushishe Ashina Momo led his tribe to settle south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were then divided. Yushishe Ashina Momo led his tribe to settle south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 蘭縱反間以離其部落，頡利果疑摸末，摸末懼，而頡利又遣兵追之，蘭率眾逆擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Lan spread a counter-plot to divide the tribes; Jieli indeed suspected Momo; Momo was afraid, and Jieli also sent troops to pursue him; Lan led his host to strike them head-on and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Lan spread disinformation to divide them. Khan Jieli suspected Momo. Momo fled in fear when Jieli sent troops after him. Lan intercepted and defeated Jieli's force.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為能，超拜豐州刺史，再轉夏州都督，封平原郡公。

translations.literal: Taizong considered him capable, promoted him beyond regular steps to Prefect of Feng, then again to Military Governor of Xia, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong judged him capable, promoted him directly to prefect of Feng, then military governor of Xia, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，以謀反腰斬。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan he was cut in two at the waist for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenguan he was executed by waist-slicing for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛大將軍丘行恭探其心肝而食之，太宗聞而召行恭讓之曰：「典刑自有常科，何至於此！

translations.literal: Right Martial Guard Grand General Qiu Xinggong dug out his heart and liver and ate them; Taizong, hearing of it, summoned Xinggong and reproved him, saying: "Statutory punishment has its regular rules—how reach to this!
translations.idiomatic: Right Martial Guard Grand General Qiu Xinggong dug out Lan's heart and liver and ate them. When Taizong heard, he summoned Qiu and rebuked him: "The law has its proper forms. How could you go this far!

sentences.zh: 必若食逆者心肝而為忠孝，則劉蘭之心為太子諸王所食，豈至卿邪？

translations.literal: If eating rebels' hearts and livers counts as loyalty and filial piety, then Liu Lan's heart should be eaten by the crown prince and the princes—would it reach you?"
translations.idiomatic: If eating a rebel's heart and liver counts as loyalty, then the crown prince and the other princes should eat Liu Lan's heart before it ever reaches you!"

sentences.zh: 」行恭無以答。

translations.literal: Xinggong had nothing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：侯君集摧凶克敵，效用居多；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Hou Junji crushed the fierce and overcame the enemy, his effective service predominating;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Hou Junji crushed fierce enemies and served with great effect;

sentences.zh: 恃寵矜功，粗率無檢，棄前功而罹後患，貪愚之將明矣。

translations.literal: relying on favor and boasting of merit, coarse and unrestrained without restraint, he abandoned former achievement and encountered later calamity—the greedy foolish general is made clear.
translations.idiomatic: yet he relied on favor, boasted of his merit, and acted without restraint. He threw away his earlier achievements and brought ruin on himself—a greedy fool of a general, plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 張亮聽公穎之妖言，恃弓長之邪讖，義兒斯畜，惡跡遂彰，雖道裕雲反狀未形，而詭詐之性，於斯驗矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang listened to Gongying's demonic words, relied on the evil prophecy of 'bow-long,' raised sworn sons in herds, and his wicked tracks were thereby revealed; though Daoyu said the signs of rebellion were not yet formed, his deceitful nature is here verified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang listened to Gongying's sorcery and trusted the prophecy of a 'lord Zhang.' He raised hundreds of sworn sons, and his wickedness was exposed. Though Li Daoyu said the evidence of rebellion was incomplete, his deceitful nature was proved.

sentences.zh: 萬徹籌深行陣，勇冠戎夷，不能保其首領，以至誅戮。

translations.literal: Wanche's stratagems ran deep in battle arrays and his courage topped the barbarians, yet he could not preserve his head and neck, ending in execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanche's tactics were deep and his courage unmatched among the frontier peoples, yet he could not save his own head and was executed.

sentences.zh: 夫二三子，非慎始而保終也。

translations.literal: These two or three men did not begin with caution and preserve their end.
translations.idiomatic: These men did not begin with caution and end in honor.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君子立功，守以謙沖。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The gentleman who establishes merit guards it with modest humility.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The gentleman who wins merit guards it with modest humility.

sentences.zh: 小人得位，足為身害。

translations.literal: The petty man who gains position has enough to harm his person.
translations.idiomatic: The petty man who gains high office courts harm to himself.

sentences.zh: 侯、張凶險，望窺聖代。

translations.literal: Hou and Zhang were fierce and dangerous, gazing to pry into the sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Hou and Zhang were violent and treacherous, scheming against the sacred age.

sentences.zh: 雄若韓、彭，難逃菹醢。

translations.literal: Heroes like Han and Peng—hard to escape minced pickle.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes like Han Xin and Peng Yue still could not escape the chopping block.
